C-65.Name: Wide tables, part 1: column widths remembered per file in the Mark profile, a table toolbar anchored to the text-column edge, a «columns X–Y of N» caption, and a per-table «Full width» mode
C-65.Summary: User review 2026-10-18 (brainstorm ~/prj/mark-media/ideas/view-modes.md): wide tables silently disappear past the column edge (macOS hides the scrollbar, the expand glyph shows only on hover and looks unlike the diagram pill), and resized column widths are lost on restart. Decisions: widths persist in the Mark profile (option 2) only after a real resize, keyed by file path, never written into the Markdown. Approved mockup 2026-10-18, variant E (https://claude.ai/artifact/EFn81ohZg6rsf4CW46AvXp): no edge arrows or chips — only an edge shade and a caption; the table toolbar and the caption are both anchored to the right edge of the text column (the invisible boundary), the toolbar ABOVE the table, the caption BELOW it, in every mode. View modes «Document» / «Notebook» are a separate later change.

Problem.Description: C-39 T-002 keeps column widths in a session-only map (lib/tableResize), so they reset on relaunch. Tables carry the standalone button.ag-block-expand glyph (C-51) while diagrams moved to the hover pill (C-56 T-005/T-007). The C-39 edge shadow is faint and there is no textual cue that columns are hidden; users read a clipped table as the whole table.

Goals.R-1: Persist column widths per file in the Mark profile (prefs/userData), written only after a user resize. Key: absolute file path + table ordinal + header signature (column count and header text hash). A changed header signature drops that table's widths; a missing or moved file never receives widths; entries for files that no longer exist are pruned (on load, bounded store size). Markdown, history and isSaved are never touched.
Goals.R-2: Rename through Mark (title-bar card › Rename… / RESPONSE_FOR_RENAME and the sidebar rename) moves the stored widths to the new path; a Finder move does not.
Goals.R-3: Double-click on a column border (existing reset gesture) also removes the stored width for that column; resetTable removes the table entry.
Goals.R-4: Table toolbar: on hover over a table figure a pill of the C-56 family appears ABOVE the table (just over its top edge), its right edge on the right edge of the text column. It may cover the end of the line above — accepted (the user is looking at the table). Buttons: «Full width» ↔ «Fit to page» (toggle, R-6) and «Open full screen» (the existing viewer). A caret in a cell does not hide it (unlike diagrams; live review 2026-10-19). Labels show on button hover like the diagram pill; localized in ten locales; keyboard focus reveals it too; the standalone table expand glyph is removed. The pill never floats over the middle of the table.
Goals.R-5: Overflow cue: while columns are hidden, an edge shade on each side that hides columns (right at the start, both in the middle, left at the end) and a caption BELOW the table, right-aligned on the same text-column edge: «columns X–Y of N» (ten locales), updated live on scroll and resize. No arrows, no chips. A table that fits shows neither shade nor caption.
Goals.R-6: Full width mode (per table): «Full width» lays the table out at its natural width, ignoring the text column: a table that fits the editor area is centred in it; a wider one starts a 24 px gutter from the editor area's left edge and makes the editor scroll horizontally (live review 2026-10-19: sticking to the window edge read as «flew off to the left»). The toolbar and caption stay on the text-column edge (inside the window); the caption reads «all N columns». The button turns into «Fit to page» (active state). The mode is remembered per table in the same profile store as the widths (R-1 keying and pruning). DEFAULT (user decision 2026-10-19): a table wider than the text column opens in Full width without anything being stored; «Fit to page» on it is an explicit per-table choice persisted as fit: true; tables that fit the column are untouched.
Goals.R-7: Tests — 100%: every new or changed module of this change at 100% line and branch coverage (vitest --coverage, per-file thresholds pinned in the config, never lowered); unit pins for width-store keying, signature drop, prune, rename move, reset paths, caption range math (start / middle / end / fits / single column), shade sides, full-width toggle and its persistence; e2e chromium + webkit-tables for every state of the approved mockup (rest, hover toolbar position against the column edge, caption alignment, scrolled-middle shades and «3–7 of 9», full width wider than the window with the window scrollbar, fit back, reload keeps widths and mode, edited header drops them); screenshot evidence in Paper and Ink. grace lint 0; graph M-012 and verification V-M-012 updated.

Constraints.Item: No Markdown mutation, no front-matter keys, no comments written into files.
Profile storage through the existing prefs/userData IPC; App Store sandbox-safe (no new entitlements).
Every GRACE-governed edit ships MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY; grace lint --assertions current = 0.

NonGoals.Item: View modes «Document» / «Notebook» (later change); full width here is per table only.
Pinning widths into the Markdown file.
BACKLOG (user 2026-10-19): a preference to change the default — «Show wide tables full width» on/off — for people who prefer fit-to-page by default; the muya option tableFullWidthDefault is the hook.

AffectedAreas.Item: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/editor.vue (width store wiring), src/renderer/src/store/editor.js (rename hook), a new renderer util for the width store

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: R-1..R-7 done; npx vitest run green with 100% line and branch coverage on the change's files; table e2e green on chromium + webkit-tables; grace lint 0.

Live check (user) against mockup variant E: resize columns, quit, reopen — widths kept; move the file in Finder — widths gone; wide table shows the shade and «columns X–Y of N»; the toolbar appears above the table on the column edge; Full width ↔ Fit to page works and is remembered.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Stored-width round trip across a reload; signature-drop and rename-move unit pins; pill and cue screenshots in Paper and Ink.
